question: Suresh sells an iron at a profit of 12%. Had he bought it for 25% less and sold it for ₹58 less, he would have made a profit of 30%. What is its cost price?

question: The cost price of 30 pens is equal to the selling price of 24 pens. What is the profit or loss percentage?
solution: Let each pen cost ₹1: then 30 cost ₹30, and 24 also sell for ₹30. Cost of those 24 = ₹24, so the profit is 6 on 24. Profit % = 6 ÷ 24 × 100 = 25% profit.
questionHi: 30 पेन का क्रय मूल्य 24 पेन के विक्रय मूल्य के बराबर है। लाभ या हानि प्रतिशत क्या है?
solutionHi: मान लें एक का क्रय मूल्य ₹1 है: 30 का ₹30, और 24 का विक्रय भी ₹30। उन 24 का क्रय मूल्य ₹24 है, अतः लाभ 24 पर 6 है। लाभ % = 6 ÷ 24 × 100 = 25% लाभ।

question: By selling 33 metres of cloth, a shopkeeper gains the selling price of 9 metres. What is his profit percentage?
solution: SP of 33 m − CP of 33 m = SP of 9 m, so CP of 33 m = SP of 24 m. The profit is 9 on 24: 9 ÷ 24 × 100 = 37.5%.

question: If a retailer sells a watch at a profit of 18% instead of a loss of 6%, he gets ₹600 more. What is its cost price?
solution: From 6% below the cost price to 18% above it is a jump of 18 + 6 = 24% of the cost price. 24% of cost = 600, so cost = 600 × 100/24 = ₹2,500.
questionHi: यदि एक खुदरा विक्रेता एक घड़ी को 6% हानि के स्थान पर 18% लाभ पर बेचता है, तो उसे ₹600 अधिक मिलते हैं। इसका क्रय मूल्य कितना है?
solutionHi: क्रय मूल्य से 6% कम से 18% अधिक तक का अंतर क्रय मूल्य का 18 + 6 = 24% है। क्रय मूल्य का 24% = 600, अतः क्रय मूल्य = 600 × 100/24 = ₹2,500।
